A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same APPLE study, with complete main text and Appendices A–H. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the equations, figures, table, and experimental evidence.

before.justification: v5 reports original experiments on active classification, volume estimation, and pose estimation, plus ablations and additional evaluations in Appendix C.

after.justification: v6 retains these original experimental results, including the main benchmark learning curves and Appendix C's ablations and CIFAR-10 evaluation.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same objective, SAC/CrossQ adaptations, dynamic reward recomputation, and shared transformer architecture. The prediction/target notation edits do not change the method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate MHSB, CircleSquare, TactileMNIST classification and volume estimation, Toolbox, and CIFAR-10. The sparse-reward and HideAndSeek CircleSquare scenarios also appear in both appendices.

E2.justification: HAM remains evaluated on MHSB and CircleSquare, while APPLE-RND remains in the same benchmark comparisons. Appendix C retains the same PPO/LSTM, pure-RL, grid-search, and no-prediction comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B and E retain the same preprocessing, episode horizons, evaluation conditions, metrics, training budgets, and HEBO tuning protocol. Descriptions crossing different page boundaries do not introduce setting changes.

E4.justification: Figure 5's exploration-efficiency analysis and Appendix C's architecture, supervision, grid-search, sparse-reward, downstream-task, and longer-HAM experiments are retained. The learned-policy case studies in Figures 8 and 12 also match.

E5.justification: Both report five seeds for the main experiments and standard-deviation shading in Figures 4 and 21. Appendix E retains single-seed hyperparameter screening; no run-count or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Reported values, learning curves, and rankings match across the main text and appendices. For example, both report final CircleSquare accuracies of 97%/96% and CIFAR-10 accuracies of 76%/73% for APPLE-SAC/APPLE-CrossQ, respectively. Figure 4's altered proportions preserve its results.

T1.justification: The formal problem, Equations (1)–(3), critic loss, and Appendix G derivation remain mathematically unchanged. The introductory prediction/target symbol correction is equivalent notation, without revised assumptions or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: a unified active-perception formulation, joint policy/perception learning, and evaluation across classification and regression tasks. No core claim changes in meaning or scope.

C2.justification: The discussion, conclusion, and Appendix D retain the same explanations of sample efficiency, CrossQ's robustness across tasks, learned exploration behaviors, and limitations involving data demands and practical deployment.

D1.justification: The code-access statement and Appendices E–F are unchanged, including Table 1's hyperparameters, JAX/Flax implementation, replay-buffer capacities, GPU specifications, and training-time information.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including comparisons with HAM/RAM and internally rewarded RL, and Appendix H's distinction from curiosity-based intrinsic rewards.

P1.justification: Section 3 standardizes prediction and target symbols to y_t and y*_t, matching the subsequent formulation; Figure 2's caption adds the target's time subscript. The version/date stamp also changes. These are local editorial corrections, with the narrative structure and appendix prose retained.

P2.justification: Figure 3 fixes awkward benchmark-label breaks, Figure 4 has shorter panels, and spacing changes reflow text, equations, and figures on pages 4–8. Raster illustrations in Figures 1, 2, and 10 are downsampled while retaining their content. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v6 modestly improves readability by resolving inconsistent prediction/target notation in Section 3 and Figure 2's caption and improving Figure 3's label formatting. These are limited presentation gains; the scientific contributions, experimental evidence, derivation, and limitations remain unchanged.
